texts.li: What began as {TALE} is a town now. {PLACE} has a wall the whole way round, a market square, a well that doesn't run dry in summer, and more families than anyone has bothered to count. {FACTION} have put it on their maps as a town in its own right.

[theirLowtech] {PLACE} has outgrown the name its first families gave it. Where {TALE} stood there are longhouses now, a smithy, a cattle pen and a great hall, and the elders of {FACTION} speak of it as one of their towns.

[theirHightech] {PLACE} has its charter: what was {TALE} a year ago is a registered town of {FACTION} now, with a council, a clinic of sorts, a trading floor and a road graded all the way to the colony's turning.

[leader] What began as {TALE} is a town now, and {X_nameDef}, who led its settlers through their first year, heads it. {PLACE} has a wall, a market square and more families than anyone has bothered to count.

summaries.li: {PLACE} is a town of {FACTION} for good, and doing well. Its people will want to settle a name and hold a first market, and they have not forgotten their first year beside the colony.
{PLACE} has outgrown its first walls, and {FACTION} count it among their towns now. It will want a name settled and a first market held, and it remembers who stood near it in its first year.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has come up to the colony's gate from {PLACE} with a question. The town's families are settling a name for it, now that it is a town and not a steading, and the colony was there for their first year.\n\nThey would take the colony's name, or the name of someone of the colony, or keep the one they have.

[first:fed] {X_nameDef} has come up to the gate from {PLACE}. The families there still talk about the food the colony sent them in their first year, when nobody else did. Now the town is settling a name for itself, and they would like the colony to have a say in it.

[first:gift] {X_nameDef} has come up to the gate from {PLACE}. The first roof in the town went up on the colony's timber, and the families have not forgotten. They are settling a name for the town now, and would take one from the colony.

[friend] {X_nameDef} has come up to the gate from {PLACE}. The town is settling a name now that it is a town, and some of its families want to name it after {A_nameDef}, whom {FACTION} remember well. They would take the colony's name instead, or keep their own, if the colony would rather.

[first:cold] {X_nameDef} has come up to the gate from {PLACE}, a little stiffly. The colony was not warm to the settlers in their first year, and they have not forgotten that either. But the town is settling its name, and {X_nameDef} says the colony was there first, so it should be asked.

li.label: Name it after the colony
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back down the road with the colony's answer. On {FACTION}'s maps from now on, the town carries the colony's name.
li.deed: gave the town at {TALE} the colony's name

li.label: Name it after {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back down the road with {A_nameDef}'s name. {A_nameDef} pretends not to be pleased, and does not manage it.
li.deed: let the town at {TALE} take {A_nameDef}'s name

li.label: Let it keep its own name
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is told the town should keep the name its own families chose. {PLACE} it stays.

texts.li: {PLACE} holds its first market day this week, and the colony is invited. Their carter is at the gate with an empty cart and an offer: a stall for the colony, and {COUNT} {THING} would sell well there, at a better price than any trader pays.\n\nThe carter would take the goods and pay for them here and now, at the market's price.

[first:trade] {PLACE} holds its first market day, and the families there remember that the colony was the first to trade with them, back when they were {TALE}. Their carter is at the gate: {COUNT} {THING} for a stall of the colony's, paid for here and now at the market's price.

[family] The {ITEM} family of {PLACE} are running the town's first market, and they want the colony there. Their carter is at the gate for {COUNT} {THING}, paid for here and now at the market's price.

li.label: Load the cart ({COUNT} {THING})
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} carries the {THING} out to the carter, who counts out the market's price and takes it down the road to the colony's stall at {PLACE}.
li.deed: kept a stall at the first market at {PLACE}

li.label: Not this time
li.outcome: The carter goes back to {PLACE} with an empty cart. There will be other market days.

texts.li: Market day at {PLACE} drew a crowd, and some of it has walked up the road to see the colony.
Some of the market crowd at {PLACE} didn't go home afterwards. A few have walked on up the road to see the colony the town keeps talking about.
[named] {PLACE} is on {FACTION}'s maps for good, under the name the colony gave it. Its families tell newcomers how the town began as {TALE}, and who was there in the first year.
[!named,first:fed] {PLACE} is a town of {FACTION} for good, with a market every week. Its families tell newcomers how the town began as {TALE}, and that the colony fed them when nobody else would.
[!named,first:sour] {PLACE} is a town of {FACTION} for good. Its families remember their first year beside the colony, and not all of it fondly, but they are neighbours now and mean to stay that way.
[!named] {PLACE} is a town of {FACTION} for good, with a market every week and a road to the colony's turning. What began as {TALE} has grown up.

[named] {PLACE} keeps the name the colony gave it, and that is how {FACTION} write it on their maps now. Newcomers ask where the name came from, and the older families tell them how the town began as {TALE}.
[!named,first:sour] {PLACE} is a town of {FACTION} for good. When its families talk about {TALE}, the colony's coldness that first year still comes up, though less often than it did.
